objective: Make readiness compose every configured read surface: a present but malformed health document withholds readiness with a bounded machine-readable reason, an absent health document keeps the documented unknown behavior, a valid event and health source still reports ready, and draining still forces not_ready regardless of health.
decision_supported: Is an instance safe to keep in rotation when the event read model is readable but the configured health document is unusable? Readiness answers for both surfaces and names the one that failed instead of silently omitting monitoring.
acceptance: A malformed present health document makes /readyz non-ready with a bounded machine-readable reason of health_source_invalid while the event source is readable.
An absent health document keeps the documented unknown behavior and does not by itself make an otherwise valid event source unready.
A valid event source and a valid health source still report ready with no reason field.
Draining forces not_ready with reason draining regardless of the health document state, including a malformed one.
The readiness body names which configured surface failed and never exposes health document contents, filesystem paths or credentials.
Tests cover malformed health, absent health, valid health, malformed event source and draining.
The packaged OpenAPI contract and its docs/api-openapi-v1.json mirror describe the composed readiness decision and the bounded reason vocabulary.

stop_conditions: the change would make a missing optional health document permanently non-ready without Owner approval
the change would report ready while a configured health endpoint is unusable
the change would require refactoring the health endpoints, the alert rules or the health document format
the change would require a control, ROS, MCU, motion or emergency-stop endpoint
readiness would keep reporting ready after termination began
a refusal or readiness body would echo health or event document contents, filesystem paths or credentials
the change requires modifying the dashboard rendering layer or its fixtures
a required modification falls outside allowed_paths
data_classification: internal; tests use synthetic monotonic snapshots and temporary directories and read no real robot, camera or credential data
model_policy: no model call; the readiness decision is deterministic boolean composition over two read-model probes
risks_and_fallbacks: Making an absent health document non-ready would be a permanent outage for a robot that never wrote health. Absent stays unknown and does not withhold readiness; only a present-but-unusable document fails closed.

Folding health into readiness could silently change the existing readiness contract for remote event-source deployments. The reason field is additive, the absent-health case stays ready, and the drain path keeps its existing not_ready verdict with the reason draining.
A readiness probe that raises would turn the probe into a 500. The composition catches any failure from the health probe and reports health_source_unavailable so readiness fails closed instead.
A failure detail could leak a path or a document excerpt to an unauthenticated probe. The reason is a fixed token from a four-value vocabulary and never carries an exception string.
Reading the health document on every readiness poll could re-parse a large file. HealthReadModel.ready() reuses the size and mtime cache, so an unchanged document is not re-ingested.
The readiness body could drift from the contract. The packaged OpenAPI and its docs mirror are updated together and the existing equality test keeps them identical.
